## How long can each body work? {#body-runtime data-chapter="2"}

| Robot | Power or quoted battery life |
|:--|:--|
| Franka Research 3 · fixed arm | External power |
| Hello Robot Stretch 4 · wheeled arm | 8 h under light computing load |
| Spot · quadruped | 90 min on average |
| Atlas · humanoid | 4 h, or 2 h with heavy lifting |

::: {.footnote}
Manufacturer figures · [Franka](https://franka.de/hubfs/Datasheet_FrankaResearch3_R02212_2.4.pdf) · [Hello Robot](https://hello-robot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/HelloRobot-DataSheet-Stretch-4-Rev5_AsLaunched.pdf) · [Spot](https://bostondynamics.com/products/spot/) · [Atlas](https://bostondynamics.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/atlas-spec-sheet.pdf)
:::


## How much payload can this arm carry? {#body-payload data-chapter="2"}

The **rated payload** tells us how much mass the arm can carry in a given pose.

| Hello Robot Stretch 4 | Rated arm payload |
|:--|:--|
| Arm extended | 2.5 kg |
| Arm retracted | 4 kg |

::: {.footnote}
[Hello Robot · Stretch 4 datasheet, rev. 5](https://hello-robot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/HelloRobot-DataSheet-Stretch-4-Rev5_AsLaunched.pdf)
:::


<!-- Chapter 3: Actuators -->

## 03 · What is inside a joint actuator? {#joint-inside data-chapter="3"}

An **actuator** converts energy into force or motion.

{{< inline-svg ../../Figures/lectures/dgist-2026f-w13/rotary-joint-parts.svg width="98%" >}}


## How does electricity turn a shaft? {#motor-field data-chapter="3"}

Current in the coils creates a magnetic field.

The motor drive changes the field as the rotor turns.


## A gear trades speed for torque {#gear-tradeoff data-chapter="3"}

| Ideal 3:1 reduction | Motor shaft | Joint shaft |
|:--|:--:|:--:|
| Turns per second | 3 | 1 |
| Torque | 1 N·m | 3 N·m |

::: {.footnote}
[Lynch & Park · Modern Robotics §8.9](https://modernrobotics.northwestern.edu/nu-gm-book-resource/8-9-actuation-gearing-and-friction/)
:::

## Can the foot move the motor? {#backdrive-qdd data-chapter="3"}

A bump moves the foot. Can that motion turn the motor shaft?

**Quasi-direct drive (QDD)** pairs a high-torque motor with a small reduction ratio.

::: {.footnote}
[MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab · Actuator design for legged robots](https://biomimetics.mit.edu/research/1a9ba04b-d200-4743-b8fc-bf231f3231f0/)
:::


## Why put a spring in a joint? {#elastic-spring data-chapter="3"}

**Motor → spring → joint**

In a **series elastic actuator (SEA)**, spring deflection helps estimate torque.

::: {.footnote}
[Pratt & Williamson · Series Elastic Actuators, IROS 1995](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/865.15/people/rebecca.kleinberger/assets/papers/SEA_Pratt.pdf)
:::


## How long can a motor pull that hard? {#motor-heat data-chapter="3"}

| CubeMars AK80-6 KV100 | Output torque |
|:--|:--:|
| Rated | 6 N·m |
| Peak | 12 N·m |

::: {.footnote}
[CubeMars · AK80-6 KV100 actuator specifications](https://www.cubemars.com/product/ak80-6-kv100-robotic-actuator.html)
:::


## Atlas changed its source of joint motion {#atlas-power data-chapter="3"}

**Hydraulic Atlas** used pressurized fluid to move its joints.

**Electric Atlas** uses motors to turn its joints.

::: {.footnote}
[Boston Dynamics · Atlas from research robot to industrial humanoid](https://bostondynamics.com/blog/atlas-evolution-from-research-robot-to-industrial-humanoid/)
:::

## What can each sensor tell us? {#body-and-world data-chapter="4"}

| Sensor | A measurement we can use |
|:---|:---|
| Inertial measurement unit (IMU) | How fast the body is turning |
| Camera | Where the next stair appears in the image |
| Fingertip pressure sensor | Where an object presses on the finger |

::: {.footnote}
[Spot · Inertial and foot-contact data](https://dev.bostondynamics.com/docs/concepts/joint_control/readme) · [Figure 03 · Palm cameras and fingertip sensing](https://www.figure.ai/news/helix-02)
:::


## Which hand fits the job? {#hand-design data-chapter="4"}

A **parallel-jaw gripper** closes its two jaws to hold a part.

**Articulated fingers** can reposition an object within the hand.

::: {.footnote}
[Franka · Gripper interface](https://frankarobotics.github.io/libfranka/0.15.0/classfranka_1_1Gripper.html) · [Boston Dynamics · Atlas hand design](https://bostondynamics.com/blog/robot-hands-for-modern-ai-and-real-work/)
:::

<!-- Chapter 5: Control -->

## 05 · How does a wheel reach its target? {#wheel-feedback data-chapter="5"}

**Open loop** · Send a timed command.

**Closed loop** · Read the wheel angle and correct the motion.

::: {.fragment}
If the wheel slows under load, which controller notices?
:::


## How much correction is left? {#proportional-correction data-chapter="5"}

Target **30°**. At **20°**, the gap is **10°**. At **28°**, it is **2°**.

::: {.fragment}
$$u = K_p(r-y)$$

Correction = gain × remaining gap.
:::

::: {.footnote}
[Stanford CS123 · One joint, one measured angle · Fall 2026 Lab 1](https://cs123-stanford.readthedocs.io/en/latest/schedule/labs/fall-26/lab-1.html)
:::

## What happens on the next shift? {#field-failure data-chapter="8"}

A pallet blocks a mobile robot's usual route.

What would you record before sending it back into the aisle?

::: {.fragment}
Load and surface · Stops and recovery · Human interventions
:::


## Why does hardware matter to Physical AI now? {#why-now data-chapter="8"}

- Affordable arms can record failures alongside successes.
- A policy can request how hard the hands should push.
- Measured motors make simulated practice more realistic.

::: {.footnote}
[ArmnetBench](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.03168v1) · [Ctrl-F](https://forcectrl.github.io/#hardware) · [Atlas](https://bostondynamics.com/blog/atlas-on-a-roll/) · [CoRL workshop, Nov 12](https://beneath-the-policy.github.io/)
:::

## What would you ask about a new robot? {#read-new-robot data-chapter="9"}

**A command is not motion.**

What was commanded? Which body moved?

What was measured? What still needs evidence?
